title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
note: arXiv record, v1 only, by Kaljevic, Arzola and Zhang; accepted to IEEE PES Grid Edge 2027. Abstract: 4 trained-from-scratch models and 4 foundation models on 3 load datasets; Chronos-2 best zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are exact or well forecast, degrades with noisier covariate forecasts, where TimesNet is more robust. No numbers in abstract; no code link on the page.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Setup: hourly load, ISO-NE 2015-2019 (temperature, dew point, day-ahead demand forecast), an anonymous North American utility 1987-1991 (temperature), CAISO 2021-2025 (ERA5 temperature, solar and wind mix). Split about 3.5 y train, 6 mo validation, 1 y test. Task called day-ahead; numeric horizon not given. Metrics MAE and MAPE. No intervals or seeds reported.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Models: DLinear, PatchTST, Informer, TimesNet trained from scratch; TimesFM 2.5, Chronos-2, Moirai 2.0, TiRex zero-shot; only Chronos-2 fine-tuned. Only Informer, TimesNet and Chronos-2 receive future covariates; the other foundation models run univariate. No checkpoint revisions given. No code or data repository; no pre-registration mentioned.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Covariate uncertainty is simulated, not archived forecasts: Gaussian noise with sd = lambda x ARIMA residual sd is added to the true future covariates, lambda in 0, 0.5, 1, 5. Authors say independent Gaussian noise is a simplification (no bias or temporal dependence). They state, from public disclosures, that the datasets are not in the models' pre-training corpora.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Table V, MAPE %, Chronos-2 zero-shot vs TimesNet, future covariates. ISO-NE: lambda 0 1.92 vs 1.91; 1 2.80 vs 2.19; 5 9.14 vs 5.17. NAU: 0 2.31 vs 2.24; 1 2.62 vs 2.47; 5 5.47 vs 5.33. CAISO: 0 2.47 vs 2.40; 1 3.25 vs 2.50; 5 5.65 vs 3.72. Fine-tuned Chronos-2 at lambda 0: 1.67, 1.99, 2.13 (best in each). Values read twice, same both times.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Table IV, history only, MAPE %: Chronos-2 zero-shot 3.44 ISO-NE, 2.86 NAU, 2.72 CAISO, the lowest zero-shot values; TimesNet 4.02, 3.14, 3.08. So exact future covariates cut Chronos-2 zero-shot MAPE from 3.44 to 1.92 on ISO-NE, and at lambda 5 it is worse than using no future covariates.
